description: Rows of checkpoint_leases (design/32-Thread-Leases.md) as any writer leaves them, and what every SQL store must make of them. expires_at is Unix milliseconds: SQLite stores the number, Postgres to_timestamp(expires_at / 1000.0). t-held is held until 2100; t-expired's lease ran out in 2000 and nobody took the thread; t-released's was given up, which clears its owner and expiry and keeps its token. 'leases' is what GetLeaseAsync / get_lease returns for each thread (null: not held), and 'next_tokens' the token the next acquisition gets (null: it is refused, the thread is held). t-never has no row.
